name: Lavandula angustifolia
description: A compact lavender with very fragrant flowers in early summer, used for oil and cooking.
care_note: Prefers cool, dry climates and often struggles in humid subtropical summers. French lavender suits those gardens better.

name: Lavandula dentata
description: A lavender with toothed grey-green leaves that flowers for most of the year in warm climates and copes with humidity better than English lavender.

name: Lavandula stoechas
description: A lavender with 'rabbit ear' bracts on top of each flower head, flowering in spring.
care_note: It self-seeds into bushland and is an environmental weed in parts of southern Australia. Please cut off the flower heads before they set seed.

name: Salvia rosmarinus
description: The culinary herb, a tough Mediterranean shrub whose blue flowers feed bees through winter and spring.

name: Salvia leucantha
description: A soft shrub with long velvety purple flower spikes through autumn and winter.
pruning: Cut flowered stems to the ground in late winter.

name: Salvia microphylla
description: A bushy salvia with small leaves and red, pink or red-and-white flowers for most of the year. 'Hot Lips' is a popular variety.

name: Gardenia jasminoides
description: An evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and very fragrant white flowers in late spring and summer. Moths pollinate it at night.
fertiliser_note: Please use an azalea and camellia food, which keeps the soil acidic.
care_note: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is too alkaline or too cold.

name: Murraya paniculata
description: A glossy hedging shrub with flushes of strongly scented white flowers from spring to autumn, followed by red berries.
care_note: Birds spread its berries into bushland, and it is considered an environmental weed in parts of Queensland and New South Wales. Please trim off the berries.

name: Hibiscus rosa-sinensis
description: The tropical hibiscus, with large, showy flowers from spring to autumn.
care_note: Hibiscus beetles and aphids attack the buds. Please pick up and bin fallen buds.

name: Bougainvillea glabra
description: A thorny climber covered in papery purple, pink or orange bracts for months in warm weather.
care_note: Very thorny. It flowers best when kept on the dry side.

name: Hydrangea macrophylla
description: A deciduous shrub with large heads of blue, pink or white flowers in summer. Most of the flowers are sterile, so they offer bees little.
pruning: Prune in late winter, cutting stems that flowered back to a pair of fat buds.
care_note: Acid soil turns most coloured varieties blue, and alkaline soil turns them pink.

name: Camellia sasanqua
description: A camellia with smaller leaves and simple flowers in autumn and early winter. It suits hedges and copes with more sun than other camellias.

name: Camellia japonica
description: A large camellia with big, often double flowers from winter into spring.

name: Agapanthus praecox
description: A clumping plant with round heads of blue or white flowers in summer.

name: Strelitzia reginae
description: A clumping plant from South Africa with orange-and-blue flowers shaped like a bird's head.

name: Plumeria rubra
description: A deciduous small tree with fragrant flowers through summer. The flowers have no nectar; they lure moths with scent alone.

toxic.note: The milky sap irritates skin and eyes.

name: Duranta erecta
description: A fast-growing shrub with drooping sprays of purple flowers in summer, followed by yellow berries. Butterflies love the flowers.

toxic.note: The yellow berries are poisonous to people and pets.

care_note: Birds spread its berries, and it is an environmental weed in parts of Queensland and New South Wales.

name: Lantana camara
description: A thorny, scrambling shrub with clusters of multicoloured flowers. It is one of Australia's worst weeds and forms dense thickets in bushland.

compost.note: Please bag it rather than composting, as stems and seeds can regrow.

toxic.note: The leaves and unripe berries are poisonous, especially to livestock.

care_note: A Weed of National Significance. Please remove it and replace it with native shrubs.

name: Gazania rigens
description: A low plant with large daisy flowers that open in sunshine.
care_note: An environmental weed of coastal areas in parts of southern Australia. Please remove spent flower heads before they set seed.

name: Nandina domestica
description: An upright shrub with lacy leaves that colour red in winter, white flowers in early summer and red berries.

toxic.note: The berries contain cyanogenic compounds that are poisonous to cats, dogs and birds.

care_note: Birds spread the berries, and it can become weedy in bushland in parts of eastern Australia.

name: Buxus sempervirens
description: A slow-growing evergreen shrub with small leaves, used for low clipped hedges.
care_note: Box blight can kill hedges in humid weather. Japanese box (Buxus microphylla) is more reliable in warm climates.

name: Pelargonium × hortorum
description: The common garden geranium, with round heads of red, pink or white flowers for most of the year.

name: Tagetes patula
description: A compact annual with orange, yellow or red flowers, widely grown among vegetables.
care_note: Grown near tomatoes, its roots release compounds that suppress some root-knot nematodes.

name: Calendula officinalis
description: A cheerful annual with orange or yellow daisy flowers through the cooler months, with edible petals.

name: Cosmos bipinnatus
description: A tall, airy annual with pink, white or crimson flowers through summer and autumn, loved by native bees.

name: Helianthus annuus
description: The tall annual sunflower. Its big flower heads feed honey bees and native bees, and its seeds feed birds.

name: Zinnia elegans
description: A summer annual with bright, long-lasting flowers that butterflies love.

name: Tropaeolum majus
description: A sprawling annual with round leaves and orange, red or yellow flowers. The leaves, flowers and seeds are edible and peppery.
care_note: Aphids and cabbage white caterpillars often prefer it to nearby vegetables, so it can work as a trap crop.

name: Borago officinalis
description: A hairy annual herb with star-shaped blue flowers that honey bees and native bees visit all day.

toxic.note: The leaves contain small amounts of pyrrolizidine alkaloids, so please eat them only occasionally.

name: Echinacea purpurea
description: A perennial with large pink-purple daisies with a raised centre in summer. Finches eat the seed heads.

name: Coreopsis lanceolata
description: A perennial with bright yellow daisies on long stems in spring and summer.
care_note: An environmental weed in parts of Queensland and New South Wales. Please remove spent flowers before they set seed.

name: Clivia miniata
description: A clumping plant for dry shade with strappy leaves and heads of orange flowers in late winter and spring.

toxic.note: All parts, especially the roots, are poisonous if eaten.

name: Monstera deliciosa
description: A climbing plant with huge split leaves. Its fruit is edible only when fully ripe.

name: Trachelospermum jasminoides
description: A twining climber or groundcover with glossy leaves and fragrant white star-shaped flowers in late spring.

name: Jasminum polyanthum
description: A vigorous climber with clusters of very fragrant white flowers from pink buds in late winter and spring.
care_note: It spreads by runners and is an environmental weed in parts of eastern Australia. Please keep it trimmed and away from bushland.

name: Ophiopogon japonicus
description: A low, dark green, grass-like groundcover for edging and shade.

name: Euphorbia milii
description: A spiny succulent shrub with small red, pink or yellow bracts for most of the year.

name: Impatiens walleriana
description: A shade-loving bedding plant with flat flowers in many colours.
care_note: It self-seeds into moist bushland and is a weed in parts of Queensland.

name: Dietes grandiflora
description: A tough clumping plant with stiff leaves and white iris-like flowers marked with yellow and mauve in spring and summer.
